scripts._data_note: Order is load-bearing. stamp-aonid CLEARS and rewrites every aon* field from map.json, so the four steps after it must follow it, not precede it: import-archive-buckets adds the 5 categories REF_SKIP used to drop AND fills those fields in on the lightweight copies stage 1 now emits; fix-aonid-collisions re-applies the repoints and deletions stamping would undo; backfill-ast-edition needs the FINAL ast files and aonIds, so it is last but one; repair-topup-prose fixes prose the top-up wrote. All are idempotent and report-only without --write. import-new-classes merges work/new-classes/*.json (necromancer, runesmith) and must run BEFORE stamp-aonid, because it stamps its own aonIds and build-map.mjs only sees a targeted merge through its 'record carries its own aonId' branch — left out of this chain, a regen DELETED both classes and all 24 of their features. It must also run AFTER split-descriptions: split REBUILDS core-descriptions.json from whatever core.json holds, so prose written by a later merger is simply not in the rebuild and both class pages came out blank. build-map rebuilds out/map.json from the core.json the merge steps just produced; it used to be a manual step, so ANY step that added records left the map stale and stamp-aonid then refused to write — aborting the chain and dropping all 24,879 aonIds plus every later step. It is idempotent and reads only committed artefacts.
